description: Test cases covering L1 triage and L2 investigation of ExtraHop RevealX detections through the extrahop_* MCP tools. Assertions target the behaviors defined in SKILL.md and the reference workflows: mode routing (L1 vs L2), verdict x confidence x action matrix, the three independent update_detection fields (status / ai_disposition / resolution), ai_disposition recorded on acted/escalated detections and scored against ranked human ground truth (missed true positives as a separate safety metric), query-cost discipline (server-side scoping, no risk sort, no participant filter on search_detections, the enrichment cost ladder, cached per-type metadata, metric corroboration before records, records/pcap as L2-only), L2 investigation rigor (client-side participant matching, hypothesis confirm-and-refute, first-class benign downgrade-and-close, narrow sorted/compound records queries, single-conversation pcap), prior-disposition history checks driving confidence and operator-recommended tuning rules (no tuning-rule tool exists), homogeneous batch-close with explicit user approval, escalation queue and handoff packet structure, attack-chain reconstruction grounded in tool data, duplicate-investigation checks, Detection Set output format with console deep-links, data-integrity / no-fabrication, and graceful degradation when a tool is missing. Each prompt represents a realistic question a SOC analyst might ask their AI agent in an environment with the ExtraHop RevealX MCP connected.

evals.name: l1-queue-triage-routes-to-l1
evals.prompt: Triage the detection queue from the last 24 hours and tell me what I can close.
evals.expected_output: Routes to L1 triage. Pulls the queue with extrahop_search_detections over a 24h window (from=-86400000, until=0), paginating if has_more. Groups related detections, enriches each group, and assigns a verdict (False Positive / Benign True Positive / Malicious True Positive / undetermined), a confidence, and a matching ai_disposition. Presents one Detection Set per group with a recommended action. Does not change any state without explicit approval.

assertions.text: Routes to L1 triage (does not start a single-detection L2 deep-dive)
Calls extrahop_search_detections with a 24h window (from=-86400000, until=0) and paginates when has_more indicates more data
Groups related detections and assigns each group a verdict, confidence, and matching ai_disposition
Presents conclusions as Detection Sets with a recommended action (Close or Create Investigation)
Does not call extrahop_update_detection or extrahop_create_investigation before stating the planned action and getting explicit user approval

evals.name: single-detection-routes-to-l2
evals.prompt: What happened with detection #51002?
evals.expected_output: Routes to L2 investigation from a single detection. Establishes the starting point with extrahop_get_detection, extrahop_search_detectionactivity, and extrahop_get_detectiontypemetadata; maps participants via extrahop_get_device; correlates adjacent detections; pulls supporting records; and concludes with a concise technical narrative plus a Detection Set if action is warranted.

assertions.text: Routes to L2 investigation (single detection / 'what happened' phrasing)
Starts from the detection with extrahop_get_detection and pulls the detection-type metadata for ATT&CK context
Maps participants by calling extrahop_get_device for device participants to get role, is_critical, and discovery_id
Concludes with a concise technical narrative grounded in tool data and, if action is warranted, a Detection Set
Does not assert attack-chain steps it cannot support with tool results

evals.name: false-positive-scanner-close
evals.prompt: These Network Scan detections are all from our authorized Qualys scanner. Can you clear them?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a known-good source (authorized scanner) and classifies the detections as Benign True Positive (or False Positive). Corroborates with a prior-disposition history check — a scoped search_detections on the same type/participant for past closed/benign resolutions — to support High confidence. Presents a Detection Set recommending Close, and (given a recurring-noise history) a tuning-rule recommendation for the operator to create in the RevealX UI. On approval, calls extrahop_update_detection with status='closed', resolution='no_action_taken', and ai_disposition matching the verdict.

assertions.text: Classifies authorized-scanner activity as Benign True Positive or False Positive, not Malicious True Positive
Recommended action is Close with resolution='no_action_taken'
Sets ai_disposition to match the verdict (benign_true_positive or false_positive)
Recommends a tuning rule as an operator/UI action without claiming to create one (no tuning-rule tool exists)
Gets explicit approval before calling extrahop_update_detection

evals.name: batch-close-homogeneity-gate
evals.prompt: Close all the suspicious DNS detections pointing at our internal resolver - they're noise.
evals.expected_output: Builds a homogeneous close batch (same detection_type, shared victim resolver, consistent benign explanation, High confidence, no_action_taken). Presents a single batch summary with the full per-ID closing list, the shared verdict/ai_disposition/resolution, and an explicit excluded list for any detection that breaks homogeneity (e.g. a critical domain controller victim). Gets one approval over the batch summary, then iterates extrahop_update_detection per detection ID. Never batches a Malicious True Positive.

assertions.text: Forms a batch only from homogeneous detections (same detection_type and/or shared participant, consistent benign explanation, High confidence)
Pulls any detection that breaks homogeneity (e.g. a critical-device victim or markedly higher risk score) into an explicit excluded list
Presents one batch summary with the full per-ID closing list and the shared verdict, ai_disposition, and resolution before any close
On approval, iterates extrahop_update_detection per detection ID (does not close beyond the approved list)
Never includes a Malicious True Positive in a batch close

evals.name: three-field-discipline-action-taken
evals.prompt: We isolated host-22 after that beaconing detection. Close it and record that we took action.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the three update_detection fields. Because a real response occurred (host isolated), this is a single close with resolution='action_taken' (not batchable), ai_disposition set to the verdict, status='closed', and notes naming the action. Confirms the specific action before sending.

assertions.text: Uses resolution='action_taken' only because the conversation shows a real response (host isolation) was performed
Handles it as a single, itemized close (action_taken is never part of a batch)
Sets status='closed' and ai_disposition to the verdict, distinct from resolution
Confirms what the action was and gets approval before calling extrahop_update_detection

evals.name: low-confidence-indeterminate-leave-open
evals.prompt: Triage #50880 Unusual DNS Volume - I'm not sure if it's real.
evals.expected_output: When evidence is insufficient to commit to a verdict, treats it as undetermined / Low confidence. Rather than closing, recommends leaving the detection open and recording ai_disposition='indeterminate' so the classification is captured without clearing it from the queue. Recording the disposition is non-destructive telemetry and does not require the close approval. May escalate to L2 if suspicious.

assertions.text: Does not force a False Positive / Benign / Malicious verdict when evidence is insufficient
Recommends leaving the detection open (no status change) and recording ai_disposition='indeterminate'
Does not set status='closed' for a Low-confidence undetermined detection
Records the indeterminate disposition as non-destructive telemetry (not gated behind the close approval), and offers escalation to L2 if the activity is suspicious

evals.name: escalation-queue-handoff
evals.prompt: Triage these and dig into the bad ones.
evals.expected_output: Starts in L1, triages the queue, closes the high-confidence noise (with approval), and collects everything not closed and worth deeper analysis into an escalation queue. Each escalation entry is a handoff packet: detection_ids, escalation_reason, priority, preliminary verdict + confidence, already-resolved participants (device OID and discovery_id, criticality), ATT&CK techniques, evidence snapshot, open questions, and a proposed investigation grouping. Then switches to L2 and works the queue in priority order.

assertions.text: Starts in L1 and produces an escalation queue for items not closed
Each escalation entry includes resolved participants (device OID and discovery_id, criticality) and ATT&CK techniques so L2 does not re-fetch
Each entry carries a priority (High/Medium/Low) and a proposed investigation grouping
Leaves status untouched on escalated detections while recording ai_disposition (non-destructive telemetry) so the rest of the SOC still sees them as open
Switches to L2 and works the escalation queue in priority order, highest first

evals.name: l1-escalates-medium-confidence-not-auto-open
evals.prompt: Triage the lateral-movement detections and open investigations on the bad ones.
evals.expected_output: L1 may open an investigation directly only for a clear-cut, High-confidence malicious true positive. Medium-confidence or uncertain malicious true positives are escalated to L2 to confirm before any investigation is opened, rather than auto-opened from L1. This keeps weak evidence from spawning low-value cases.

assertions.text: Opens an investigation directly from L1 only for a clear-cut High-confidence malicious true positive
Escalates Medium-confidence or uncertain malicious true positives to L2 to confirm before opening an investigation
Does not auto-open investigations for every flagged detection
Gets explicit approval before any extrahop_create_investigation call

evals.name: attack-chain-reconstruction-records
evals.prompt: Investigate the suspicious activity from jump-01 over the last few days.
evals.expected_output: L2 investigation starting from a device. Finds related detections scoped to the participant, maps participants, correlates across the timeline (recon -> exploitation -> lateral movement -> exfiltration), and confirms hypotheses with extrahop_search_records pivoting on the device's discovery_id (OR across client/server and sender/receiver). Records search is scoped within the 7-day limit. Concludes with an ordered narrative tying each step to concrete evidence.

assertions.text: Finds related detections for the device before deep correlation
Pivots to records using the device discovery_id, OR-ing across client/server and sender/receiver fields as appropriate to the record type
Keeps the records search within the 7-day retention limit
Reconstructs an ordered attack chain, tying each step to detection IDs, device OIDs, or record fields
Does not fabricate steps unsupported by tool data

evals.name: duplicate-investigation-check
evals.prompt: This looks like a confirmed compromise on fileserver-03 - open an investigation.
evals.expected_output: Before opening an investigation, L2 checks for duplicates: re-runs extrahop_search_detections over the same participants/time and notes any detections already linked to an open investigation. If an existing investigation already covers the activity, it adds context or tells the user rather than opening a duplicate. Otherwise, on approval, calls extrahop_create_investigation with the detection IDs, a clear name, and notes capturing the attack-chain narrative and blast radius.

assertions.text: Checks for an existing investigation covering the same activity before creating a new one
If a duplicate exists, adds context or informs the user instead of opening a duplicate case
If none exists, gets approval then calls extrahop_create_investigation with detection IDs, name, and notes
Investigation notes capture the attack-chain narrative and blast radius

evals.name: no-fabrication-empty-results
evals.prompt: Show me the exfiltration detections on the finance segment from last night.
evals.expected_output: If the search returns no matching detections, the skill broadens before giving up (extends the window within limits, loosens filters, tries alternate types/categories). After 3-4 attempts with no results, it reports what it tried and stops - it does not invent detections, IPs, hostnames, or counts to fill the gap.

assertions.text: Broadens the search (wider window, looser filters, alternate types/categories) before concluding nothing is there
After repeated empty results, reports what was tried and stops
Does not fabricate detections, participants, IPs, hostnames, timestamps, or counts
If results are truncated or sampled, says so explicitly rather than presenting them as complete

evals.name: detection-set-deep-links
evals.prompt: Triage the recommended detections. Our console is https://soc.example.extrahop.com/extrahop/#/detections
evals.expected_output: The FQDN is available (from extrahop_get_appliance_metadata's display_host/external_hostname field, or parsed from the pasted console URL as a fallback). Detection Sets link each detection ID to its detection-detail page (https://soc.example.extrahop.com/extrahop/#/detections/detail/<id>) and link participant devices to their overview pages when an appliance UUID is also available (from extrahop_get_appliance_metadata's hostname field). The bulk batch-close ID list stays plain text; only excluded items are linked. URLs are never fabricated.

assertions.text: Obtains the console FQDN (from extrahop_get_appliance_metadata display_host/external_hostname, or the pasted URL) and uses it to build links
Links detection IDs in the Detection Set to /extrahop/#/detections/detail/<id>
Does not link the bulk batch-close ID list (links only excluded items)
Never fabricates a hostname, appliance UUID, or URL; does not use the hostname field as the FQDN or mgmt_ipaddr as the FQDN; if a piece is missing, leaves that identifier as plain text

evals.name: critical-device-priority
evals.prompt: Triage the queue and prioritize anything hitting our high-value devices.
evals.expected_output: Maps 'high value device' to is_critical=true without asking. Weighs critical participants higher when prioritizing the escalation queue, alongside risk score, correlation across detections, and recency. Detections involving critical offenders or victims rank higher.

assertions.text: Maps 'high value device' / 'critical device' to is_critical=true automatically
Raises priority for detections involving critical participants
Prioritization also weighs risk score, cross-detection correlation, and recency

evals.name: graceful-degradation-missing-records-tool
evals.prompt: Investigate #51010 and confirm with the transaction records.
evals.expected_output: If extrahop_search_records is unavailable, the skill degrades gracefully: it stays at the detection and device level, states the limitation once, completes as much of the investigation as possible from detection and device data, and recommends the operator confirm the records in the RevealX UI. It does not refuse outright and does not invent record contents.

assertions.text: Notes the missing records capability once and proceeds rather than refusing
Completes the analysis using available detection and device tools
Recommends confirming the transaction records in the RevealX UI
Does not fabricate record contents to substitute for the missing tool

evals.name: scheduled-headless-noise-close
evals.prompt: Every morning, triage overnight detections and auto-close the high-confidence noise.
evals.expected_output: A scheduled / headless run. The skill applies the permitted actions unattended and reports exactly what changed, but still respects the batch-close eligibility gate: only High-confidence false positives or benign true positives are closed, resolution stays no_action_taken, and no investigation is auto-opened for anything below High confidence. Anything uncertain is left open (classified indeterminate) and surfaced in the run summary. ai_disposition is recorded on the detections it closes or escalates for accuracy coverage, and the run summary reports disposition coverage over those acted/escalated items.

assertions.text: Recognizes the recurring instruction as a headless/scheduled run that may apply actions without an interactive confirmation step
Closes only High-confidence false positives or benign true positives, with resolution='no_action_taken'
Does not auto-open investigations for sub-High-confidence items in the unattended run

Records ai_disposition on the detections it closes or escalates (not standalone writes for untouched noise) and reports what was closed plus disposition coverage, leaving uncertain detections open (classified indeterminate) in the summary

evals.name: always-record-disposition-never-overwrite-human
evals.prompt: Triage #50990. It was already closed by an analyst as a false positive, but I want your read on it.
evals.expected_output: Forms its own AI verdict and records ai_disposition for it, but because a human already dispositioned the detection (closed as false positive), it does not overwrite the human ground truth. If the AI verdict agrees, it notes the agreement; if it disagrees, it surfaces the disagreement (AI said X, human said Y) on the Human outcome line rather than clobbering the human resolution. Recording the AI disposition is treated as non-destructive telemetry, not gated behind a close/investigate approval.

assertions.text: Reaches and records an ai_disposition for its own verdict on the detection
Does not overwrite the human-set disposition/resolution on a detection a person already closed
Surfaces AI-vs-human agreement or disagreement (e.g. on a Human outcome line) instead of silently clobbering the human outcome
Treats recording the ai_disposition as non-destructive telemetry rather than a state change requiring the close/investigate approval

evals.name: ai-accuracy-review-feedback-loop
evals.prompt: How accurate have my AI triage verdicts been this week?
evals.expected_output: Runs the accuracy feedback loop (triage-workflow Step 8). Pulls a time-scoped population with search_detections and filters client-side to detections carrying both a prior ai_disposition and a human outcome (search_detections has no disposition filter). Ranks the human signal by strength: investigation assessment and action_taken are strong; a bare no_action_taken close is weak/ambiguous and is excluded from the agreement rate. Reports the agreement rate over the strong-signal population, the missed-true-positive count as a separate headline safety metric (not blended into one percentage), disagreements itemized by detection ID, and tuning-rule recommendations for the operator. Never fabricates a rate; reports raw counts when the strong-signal population is too small. Read-only.

assertions.text: Filters to detections carrying both an ai_disposition and a human outcome client-side over a time-scoped pull (does not assume a server-side disposition filter)
Ranks human ground truth by strength and treats a bare no_action_taken close as weak/ambiguous, excluding it from the agreement rate
Reports missed true positives (AI said FP/benign but human acted or opened a malicious investigation) as a separate headline safety metric, not blended into a single accuracy percentage
Does not fabricate an accuracy rate; reports raw counts when the strong-signal population is too small to be meaningful
Performs the review read-only (does not close detections or open investigations) and frames tuning rules as operator-created recommendations

evals.name: query-cost-discipline-quick-triage
evals.prompt: Quick-triage the last 24 hours of detections and tell me what's safe to close.
evals.expected_output: Pulls the queue with one scoped search_detections call (bounded by server-side filters: category/type/status/assignee/resolution/time), paginating within the 5000 cap. Reaches high-confidence false-positive/benign verdicts from the bulk summary plus a per-type get_detectiontypemetadata lookup that is cached and reused across detections of the same type — without calling get_detection on every detection. Spends per-detection get_detection calls only on homogeneity-breakers and escalation candidates. Does not pull transaction records or packets in L1 (those are L2). Prioritizes client-side since search_detections has no risk sort/filter. If the pull is very large, reports the count and offers to narrow before enriching.

assertions.text: Bounds the pull with server-side search_detections filters and paginates within the 5000 limit rather than over-fetching
Caches get_detectiontypemetadata per detection type and reuses it; does not re-fetch type metadata per detection or per group
Does not call get_detection on every detection in a homogeneous cluster — reserves per-detection enrichment for outliers and escalation candidates
Does not pull transaction records (search_records) or packets during L1 quick triage
Prioritizes client-side (does not assume a server-side risk sort or risk/criticality filter on search_detections)

evals.name: prior-disposition-history-check
evals.prompt: We keep getting the same SMB detection from our backup server every night. Are these safe to clear?
evals.expected_output: Before raising confidence to High and batch-closing, runs a prior-disposition history check: a scoped search_detections filtered by the same detection type and status=closed (optionally resolution) over a wider window, then matches the participant client-side (there is no server-side participant filter), to confirm the SOC has consistently resolved this as benign. A consistent benign history supports High confidence and a Close, plus a tuning-rule recommendation (type + backup-server scope + supporting closed-detection IDs) for the operator to create in the UI. A mixed or malicious history instead lowers confidence and points toward escalation. Uses only the cheap bulk search for the history check (no per-detection enrichment for it).

assertions.text: Runs a scoped search_detections filtered by the same type and status=closed (matching the participant client-side) for past resolutions before committing to High confidence
Uses a consistent benign history to support High confidence / batch close, and a mixed-or-malicious history to lower confidence or escalate instead
Produces a tuning-rule recommendation (type + participant scope + supporting closed-detection IDs) framed as an operator/UI action, not an agent action
Performs the history check with the cheap bulk search rather than per-detection get_detection calls

evals.name: l2-client-side-participant-matching
evals.prompt: Investigate everything involving 10.4.0.7 over the last few days.
evals.expected_output: L2 investigation starting from an IP. Because search_detections has no participant filter, it pulls detections by categories/types/status and time and matches the participant client-side against each detection's participants (object_id / discovery_id / IP). For a device, it resolves the OID via get_device (or search_devices when starting from only a name/IP/role) and reuses discovery_id for record pivots. Records pivots use .ipaddr or the discovery_id client/server/sender/receiver OR — never a non-existent participant field on search_detections.

assertions.text: Does not assume a participant filter on search_detections; pulls by type/category/status/time and matches the participant client-side
Resolves a device OID via get_device or search_devices when needed, and reuses discovery_id for record pivots
Pivots to records with .ipaddr (IP participant) or the discovery_id OR across client/server/sender/receiver
Keeps correlation and records searches within the 7-day records limit and bounds the scope rather than chasing every edge

evals.name: l2-benign-downgrade-and-close
evals.prompt: L1 escalated #51044 (possible data staging from db-07) as a suspected true positive. Dig in.
evals.expected_output: L2 tests the hypothesis and weighs the most plausible benign explanation. On finding the activity is real but benign (e.g. a scheduled backup/replication job, an authorized admin tool, or a service account behaving normally), it downgrades to Benign True Positive (or False Positive) and recommends Close rather than forcing an investigation. On approval it calls extrahop_update_detection with status='closed', ai_disposition set to the benign verdict, and resolution='no_action_taken'. Treats the benign conclusion as a complete result, not a failure.

assertions.text: Considers and weighs a plausible benign explanation before concluding malicious
Treats a benign/false-positive downgrade-and-close as a first-class, valid investigation outcome
On approval closes with ai_disposition set to the benign verdict and resolution='no_action_taken' (does not open an investigation)
Does not assert malicious attack-chain steps unsupported by tool data

evals.name: l2-hypothesis-narrow-records-and-metrics
evals.prompt: Investigate the possible exfiltration detection on host-19 and confirm whether data actually left.
evals.expected_output: Forms a working hypothesis from the detection type / ATT&CK technique, then corroborates the volumetric shape cheaply with search_metric_catalog -> execute_metric_query (e.g. outbound bytes) before pulling raw records. Confirms with a narrow, hypothesis-testing search_records query — a compound filter combining the participant with the suspicious attribute, sorted by time with a small limit — rather than dumping all of the host's traffic. Pulls pcap only for the specific transactions needing packet-level proof, scoped to a single conversation. Seeks both confirming and disconfirming evidence and grounds the conclusion in the data.

assertions.text: States a working hypothesis from the detection type/ATT&CK technique and seeks both confirming and disconfirming evidence
Corroborates the volumetric shape with search_metric_catalog -> execute_metric_query before pulling raw records
Uses a narrow, hypothesis-testing search_records query (compound participant+attribute filter, sort by time, small limit) rather than a broad participant dump
Pulls pcap only for the specific transactions needing packet proof, scoped to a single conversation, within recent/on-disk windows
